newsitem.title: USA: K.C. Southern, Mexican partner get funds.
newsitem.headline: K.C. Southern, Mexican partner get funds.

text.p: Kansas City Southern Industries Inc and Transportacion Maritima Mexicana SA de CV. said Friday they have arranged financing for a previously announced $1.4 billion Mexican rail deal.
The two partners said Morgan Stanley will provide financing to buy a portion of the Mexican national rail system known as Ferrocarril del Noreste, or the Northeast Railroad.

The companies said their jointly controlled venture, Transportacion Ferroviaria Mexicana (TFM), deposited $560 million with the Mexican government as the initial installment under the contract to purchase the concession.
The remaining portion is expected to be paid no later than July 16, 1997.

The companies said Morgan Stanley will provide financing that includes a senior bank facility and a high yield bridge loan facility. Together with equity contributions from other parties, the financing is expected to fund the entire purchase price, they added.
TFM expects to make a high yield bond offering to be used in place of the bridge loan, the companies said.

Kansas City Southern said the Northeast Line is an active railroad corridor between Mexico City and the border crossings of Matamoros and Nuevo Laredo, which is a large commercial rail exchange between the United States and Mexico.
